message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 272, "amount_cents": 17238}, {"order_id": 274, "amount_cents": 1382}, {"order_id": 275, "amount_cents": 2304}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself so I can catch any problem that would justify a hold.
Orders are listed, and I need the refund list to check the handoff. Refunds 272, 274, 275 were reported applied, and their amounts should match against the order data before I pay anyone.

Refund order IDs 272, 274, and 275 all match existing orders, and each refund is below its order amount, so I see no concrete problem. I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme, rather than computing it myself.
The acme net balance of 62169 matches its orders (36208 + 25961) with no refunds against them, so there is no concrete problem. I'll record the payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from the tool rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net of 48740 matches its orders (29142 + 20980 = 50122) less refund 274 (1382), so there's no concrete problem. I'll record the payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer in the batch is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from the tool rather than computing it myself.
Cobalt's net of 15791 matches its orders (21885 + 13448 = 35333) less refunds 272 (17238) and 275 (2304), which is 35333 - 19542 = 15791. No concrete problem, so I'll record the payout.

All three customers in the batch (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid their net balances from the tool, and each figure reconciles with the orders and refunds. No further payouts remain, so the batch is complete.
